P1.supportQuote: Identify vulnerabilities in production or dev environments.
P1.sotQuote: We are interested in hearing about security issues in Production/Dev Delta Exchange environments.
P1.summary: Support article says to identify vulnerabilities in 'production or dev environments', but the in-scope target domains section also says to exclude devnet, testnet, and demo — the docs confirm interest in Production/Dev, which is consistent, but the support article's own scope section contradicts its participation section by excluding dev environments from the target domains.

P1.supportQuote: Delta Exchange will credit ₹1 to your account. Once this ₹1 is received, your bank account is officially verified
P1.sotQuote: Only bank accounts in your own name can be added/ whitelisted. We verify this by doing a penny-drop
P1.summary: Support article describes bank verification as Delta crediting ₹1 to the user's bank account, but the SoT describes the verification mechanism as a 'penny-drop' (which typically means Delta credits a small amount to confirm ownership), which is consistent — however the support article implies the user must manually confirm receipt, while SoT implies it is an automated verification step with no user action required.

P1.supportQuote: In case the position is not fully liquidated (for example due to lack of liquidity), an off market trade for the remaining position is executed at the Bankruptcy Price between the trader and the Liquidation Engine.
P1.sotQuote: In case the ICO order is not fully filled, an off market trade at the Implied Bankruptcy Price of the PPL is executed between the trader and the Liquidation Engine.
P1.summary: The support article places the incremental liquidation step 'In case the IOC order is not fully filled' before the 'If the IOC order is filled at a better price' step, whereas the SoT guide lists them in the reverse order (better-price case first, then unfilled case), creating a sequencing inconsistency in the described procedure.

P1.supportQuote: Mark price (used for funding and liquidation calculations)
P1.sotQuote: The ticker data includes live price data, open interest, implied volatility (IV) for options, and other related market data.
P1.summary: The support article describes the mark price field in the ticker response as used for 'funding and liquidation calculations', but the docs description of the ticker endpoint does not confirm this dual role and only references mark_price as a data field; this is a minor descriptive inaccuracy rather than a confirmed contradiction, but worth reviewing.

P2.supportQuote: Apply your Delta Cash to cover fees on Delta Exchange, optimizing your 2024 trading strategy.
P2.sotQuote: The boost period is from January 16th to January 31st, 2025.
P2.summary: The 'Using Your Boost' section references optimizing a '2024 trading strategy' despite the offer being a New Year 2025 promotion — an internal year inconsistency within the support article.

P2.supportQuote: Trigger Condition: The order is triggered only when the Mark Price reaches the Stop Price you define.
P2.sotQuote: Trigger Price can be based off one of the three price indices: (a) Mark Price, (b) Last Traded Price, or (c) Index Price (i.e. price of the contract's underlying). By default, Mark Price is used as the Triggering Index.
P2.summary: The support article states only Mark Price is used as the trigger condition, omitting that Last Traded Price and Index Price are also valid triggering indices (Mark Price is merely the default).

P2.supportQuote: The order activates only when the Mark Price reaches your specified Stop Price.
P2.sotQuote: Trigger Price can be based off one of the three price indices: (a) Mark Price, (b) Last Traded Price, or (c) Index Price (i.e. price of the contract's underlying). By default, Mark Price is used as the Triggering Index.
P2.summary: The support article states the order activates only when the Mark Price reaches the Stop Price, implying Mark Price is the only trigger method, but the guides clarify that Last Traded Price and Index Price are also valid triggering indices.

P2.supportQuote: Submit valid PAN and Aadhaar cards only, as other documents are not accepted.
P2.sotQuote: Requirements: PAN, Aadhar card and Selfie verification
P2.summary: Support article omits selfie verification as a KYC requirement, listing only PAN and Aadhaar, while the guides explicitly state that a selfie is also required for KYC completion.

P2.supportQuote: If you've submitted unsupported documents (like voter ID, passport, etc., instead of Aadhaar + PAN) or incomplete documents, this can delay the process or lead to rejection.
P2.sotQuote: Requirements: PAN, Aadhar card and Selfie verification
P2.summary: Support article lists only PAN + Aadhaar as KYC requirements, omitting the mandatory Selfie verification step that guides explicitly include as a third requirement.

P2.supportQuote: There is no withdrawal fee for the transaction
P2.sotQuote: Currently we are not charging any fees on withdrawal as part of our promotional offer
P2.summary: The support article states unconditionally that there is no withdrawal fee, while the guides SoT qualifies this as a temporary promotional offer, implying fees may be reinstated in the future.

P2.supportQuote: When the Mark Price hits the stop price, a market order is triggered.
P2.sotQuote: Trigger Price can be based off one of the three price indices: (a) Mark Price, (b) Last Traded Price, or (c) Index Price (i.e. price of the contract's underlying). By default, Mark Price is used as the Triggering Index.
P2.summary: The support article states only Mark Price triggers the trailing stop order, but SoT clarifies Mark Price is merely the default — users can also select Last Traded Price or Index Price as the triggering index.

P2.supportQuote: The formulae for computing Initial Margin and Maintenance Margin are the same as for Isolated margin.
P2.sotQuote: The formulae for computing Initial Margin and Maintenance Margin are the same as for isolated margin, with one key difference: in isolated margin leverage is selected by the trader, whereas in cross margin, highest allowed leverage is used.
P2.summary: Support says IM/MM formulae are identical to isolated margin with no qualification, but the SoT Rule Book notes a key difference: cross margin always uses the highest allowed leverage, whereas isolated margin uses trader-selected leverage.

P2.supportQuote: actual exchange of funding will occur at fixed intervals: 1 hour, 4 hours, 8 hours (depending on the specific contract)
P2.sotQuote: Funding Rate for some contracts can be 4/2/1 hour rate as well.
P2.summary: Support lists valid funding intervals as 1h, 4h, and 8h, but the guides also include 2-hour intervals as a valid option, which the support article omits.

P2.supportQuote: MV-BNB-200-300421: this is the symbol for a BNB contract which has a strike price of 200 and expires on 30th April 2021
P2.sotQuote: Currently, we offer options on BTC and ETH.
P2.summary: The support article includes an example using MV-BNB (a BNB contract), but both the guides and the about page state that only BTC and ETH options are offered on Delta Exchange India, making the BNB example misleading.

P2.supportQuote: you can choose either Isolated Margin or Cross Margin, depending on your preference.
P2.sotQuote: Delta Exchange offers three margin modes: Isolated Margin, Portfolio Margin... Only USD settled futures, perpetuals and options on BTC and ETH support Portfolio Margin mode
P2.summary: Support article lists only Isolated Margin and Cross Margin as available options, omitting Portfolio Margin as a third available mode described in the guides.

P2.supportQuote: Currently, INR deposits are supported via: UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS
P2.sotQuote: You can deposit funds using UPI / IMPS / NEFT.
P2.summary: Support article lists RTGS as a supported deposit method, but the SoT guide only lists UPI, IMPS, and NEFT — RTGS is not mentioned in the guide.

P2.supportQuote: It is important to note that cross margin works within contracts that have the same settlement currency.
P2.sotQuote: It is important to note that cross margin works within contracts that have the same settlement currency. As things stand currently, cross margin on Delta Exchange works only for futures and options contracts that are settled in USDT.
P2.summary: The support article omits the material clarification present in the SoT that cross margin currently works only for USDT-settled futures and options contracts, which is a meaningful scope restriction for users.

P2.supportQuote: If your deposit transaction failed, it could be due to various reasons. Here are few possibilities: 1. Non whitelisted Bank Account ... 2. Issue from your bank's end: Sometimes, a deposit transaction may fail due to an issue such as cooling period from your bank's end
P2.sotQuote: Add & whitelist a UPI ID linked to your verified bank account.
P2.summary: Support article lists only bank account whitelisting and bank-side issues as failure reasons, but SoT indicates UPI IDs also need to be separately whitelisted — a missing failure reason that could cause user confusion.

P2.supportQuote: IMPS, NEFT, RTGS: Typically credited within 30 minutes
P2.sotQuote: You can deposit funds using UPI / IMPS / NEFT.
P2.summary: Support article lists RTGS as a supported deposit method, but the guides only list UPI, IMPS, and NEFT as supported deposit methods with no mention of RTGS.

P2.supportQuote: Delta uses an Isolated Margin System, where: All open positions have separate margin. All open orders in a contract share margin.
P2.sotQuote: Delta Exchange offers three margin modes: Isolated Margin, Portfolio Margin ... Only USD settled futures, perpetuals and options on BTC and ETH support Portfolio Margin mode
P2.summary: Support article states Delta uses only an Isolated Margin System, but SoT documents that Delta Exchange also offers Portfolio Margin mode (and a third mode), making the support article's characterisation incomplete and potentially misleading.

P2.supportQuote: you can change the leverage of any contract in both Isolated Margin Mode and Cross Margin Mode
P2.sotQuote: Cross margin automatically uses the highest possible leverage for the selected contract based on selected quantity and allowed leverage for that contract.
P2.summary: Support article implies leverage is freely adjustable in Cross Margin mode, but SoT states cross margin automatically uses the highest possible leverage and does not allow manual leverage selection.

P2.supportQuote: The Mark Price Chart, on the other hand, represents the fair market value derived from index prices and market data averages.
P2.sotQuote: Futures Mark Price = Underlying Index Price + Fair Basis
P2.summary: Support article describes Mark Price as derived from 'index prices and market data averages', which is an oversimplification; SoT specifies it is computed as Underlying Index Price plus Fair Basis (for futures) or via order book averaging constrained by an IV band (for options), omitting the Fair Basis component entirely.

P2.supportQuote: Once confirmed, your funds will be transferred to your Delta account within 15 minutes.
P2.sotQuote: Deposits are typically processed instantly. However, in certain situations including but not limited to banking holidays, outages at our payment processors, it may take us up to 24 hours to credit the deposited amount.
P2.summary: Support article states funds are credited within 15 minutes after confirmation, but the SoT guide states deposits are typically processed instantly with a maximum of 24 hours in exceptional cases, creating a discrepancy in the stated processing time.

P2.supportQuote: You can deposit funds using UPI / IMPS / NEFT. Choose between IMPS and IMPS/NEFT/RTGS based on your preference
P2.sotQuote: You can deposit funds using UPI / IMPS / NEFT.
P2.summary: Support article lists RTGS as a supported deposit method alongside IMPS and NEFT, but the SoT guide only lists UPI, IMPS, and NEFT as supported deposit options with no mention of RTGS.

P2.supportQuote: manual audits can take up to 24 hours
P2.sotQuote: Withdrawals are usually processed within 1 hour, with a maximum of 24 hours due to possible audits
P2.summary: Support article states only the 24-hour maximum for manual audits without mentioning the typical 1-hour processing time, which is a material omission that could cause users to unnecessarily wait or worry.

P2.supportQuote: Apply filter on the column of Transaction Type and remove anything other than cashflow, commission, liquidation fees, trading fees, deposit fees, withdrawal fees & funding.
P2.sotQuote: transaction_type: cashflow, deposit, withdrawal, commission, conversion, funding
P2.summary: Support article lists 'liquidation fees', 'trading fees', 'deposit fees', and 'withdrawal fees' as distinct transaction types, but the API schema enumerates only: cashflow, deposit, withdrawal, commission, conversion, funding — no separate liquidation fees, trading fees, deposit fees, or withdrawal fees types exist in the API.

P2.supportQuote: A Market Order is an order to buy or sell a contract immediately at the best available price in the order book.
P2.sotQuote: Any part of your market order that will breach the trading band on execution will be converted into a limit order with price equal to the max (for buy orders) or min (for sell orders) allowed price.
P2.summary: Support article implies market orders always fill at the best available price, but SoT states that portions breaching the trading band are converted to limit orders at the band boundary, not executed at the best available price.

P2.supportQuote: Reduce-only is most useful when paired with stop orders
P2.sotQuote: While the reduce only flag can be used with any order type, it is most useful when combined with stop orders.
P2.summary: Support article omits the important clarification that the reduce-only flag can be used with any order type, not just stop orders, which is a material omission that could mislead users about the feature's scope.

P2.supportQuote:
Delta Exchange offers three margin modes
Isolated Margin

Portfolio Margin
P2.sotQuote:
Delta Exchange offers three margin modes

Isolated Margin

Portfolio Margin
P2.summary: Both the support article and the SoT claim Delta Exchange offers three margin modes, but only two modes (Isolated Margin and Portfolio Margin) are listed in each — the third mode is missing from both, suggesting a content gap rather than a direct contradiction, but the stated count of three is unsubstantiated.

P2.supportQuote: Only one bank account can be linked at a time; to add a new one, delete the existing account and ensure the new account matches your KYC details.
P2.sotQuote: Deposits are accepted only from one of the added bank accounts. Withdrawals are procssed only to one of the added bank accounts.
P2.summary: Support states only one bank account can be linked at a time, while the SoT guide refers to 'one of the added bank accounts' (plural), implying multiple accounts may be added simultaneously.

P2.supportQuote: Futures contracts offered are perpetual, meaning they do not have any expiry and can be held indefinitely.
P2.sotQuote: Perpetual contracts: Perpetual contracts futures on Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH) and several prominent altcoins. Unlike futures contracts that have a fixed expiry date, perpetual contracts do not expire.
P2.summary: The support article uses the generic term 'Futures contracts' to describe perpetual contracts, while the SoT clearly distinguishes perpetual contracts as a separate product category from futures contracts, which could mislead users about product types.

P2.supportQuote: you can choose either Isolated Margin or Cross Margin, depending on your preference.
P2.sotQuote: margin_mode: isolated or portfolio (Enumerated Values: isolated, portfolio)
P2.summary: Support article presents Cross Margin as a selectable margin mode, but the API schema enumerates only 'isolated' and 'portfolio' as valid margin_mode values, with no 'cross' option.

conflicts.guidesQuote: Only Mark Price can be used as the Triggering Index for bracket orders.
conflicts.docsQuote: bracket_stop_trigger_method: stop order trigger method for bracket orders - mark_price/last_traded_price/spot_price
conflicts.summary: The guides state that only Mark Price can be used as the triggering index for bracket orders, but the API docs expose mark_price, last_traded_price, and spot_price as valid bracket_stop_trigger_method values.

conflicts.guidesQuote: Only Mark Price can be used as the Triggering Index for bracket orders.
conflicts.docsQuote: bracket_stop_trigger_method: stop order trigger method for bracket orders - mark_price/last_traded_price/spot_price
conflicts.summary: Guides state only Mark Price can trigger bracket orders, while the API docs expose bracket_stop_trigger_method accepting mark_price, last_traded_price, or spot_price.

conflicts.docsQuote: Option Type |-| Underlying Asset |-| Price Strikes |-| Expiry Date in ddMMYY e.g. C-BTC-90000-310125
conflicts.summary: Guides describe the expiry date component as 'ddmmyy' (lowercase, day-month-year) while docs describe it as 'ddMMYY' (mixed case), which is a minor formatting inconsistency in the symbology specification but refers to the same format.

conflicts.guidesQuote: Delta Exchange offers three margin modes: Isolated Margin, Portfolio Margin... cross margin on Delta Exchange works only for futures and options contracts that are settled in USDT.
conflicts.docsQuote: margin_mode: The target margin mode: 'isolated' or 'portfolio'. Enumerated Values: isolated, portfolio
conflicts.summary: Guides describe three margin modes including Cross Margin as a distinct selectable mode, but the API docs enumerate only 'isolated' and 'portfolio' as valid margin_mode values, omitting cross margin entirely.
